clue.text: Range of largely unqualified opinion

indicators.note: largely means most of the word but not all of it, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: unqualified means pure, absolute, with no reservations
an opinion is a view

explanation.surface: Someone surveys the spread of views that are mostly unreserved.
explanation.definitionFit: A purview is the scope or extent of something's concern or authority.

clue.text: Endeavour to support writer producing The Raven, for example

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits underneath the other

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American author
an endeavour is a try

explanation.surface: An attempt backs up the author who wrote The Raven.
explanation.definitionFit: Poe's famous work is a poem, and poems collectively are verse.

clue.text: Upset publicity head — nothing right round house

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in this down answer the letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: AD is short for advertisement, publicity
nut is slang for the head
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A publicist is upset, with nothing right around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns AD+NUT+O+R, giving the answer read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular building, usually domed, is a round house in plain description.

clue.text: Reformed erotomaniac, having rejected extremes

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the remaining letters are rearranged
dropping the extremes means losing the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A sex addict who has mended his ways and given up his excesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having rejected extremes' takes off E and C, leaving ROTOMANIA, which 'Reformed' rearranges; the result is a fitting description of a tamed lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A male lover or sweetheart, a gentler figure than an obsessive.

clue.text: Tribal magician asking advice on medical care?

explanation.surface: A shaman wonders which physician to consult.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading sounds like 'Which doctor?', a patient asking whom to see.
explanation.definitionFit: A healer using magic in a traditional society; also a pun on a question about choosing a physician.

clue.text: Sporting person at a German school, presumably

definitions.text: Sporting person at a German school, presumably

parts.words: Sporting person at a German school, presumably
parts.note: a German grammar school is a Gymnasium, so a pupil there might whimsically be named after the athlete who works out in a gym

explanation.surface: A sports-mad pupil at a school in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete who performs vaults and floor exercises; the German secondary school called a Gymnasium supplies the joke.

clue.text: Empty talk may have us laughing in the theatre

definitions.text: may have us laughing in the theatre

explanation.surface: Idle chatter can make an audience laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' is the operating theatre, where laughing gas (nitrous oxide) was an anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle chatter is hot air; nitrous oxide, the anaesthetic used in surgery, is known as laughing vapour.

clue.text: They inspire writing about ritual and liturgy

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
a use is a local form of church service, as in the Sarum Use

explanation.surface: Some people are moved to write on church ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: The nine goddesses of Greek myth were sources of artistic inspiration.

clue.text: Plant provides an Oriental with endless cash

parts.note: E is short for east, the Orient

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: A flower is given to an Easterner along with limitless funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering plant of the buttercup family, also called windflower.

clue.text: Ragged as one who kissed the maiden all forlorn

definitions.text: as one who kissed the maiden all forlorn

explanation.surface: A scruffy man who kissed a sad girl.
explanation.walkthrough: From the nursery rhyme The House That Jack Built: 'the man all tattered and torn, that kissed the maiden all forlorn'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragged clothes are torn and shabby; the rhyme's man was described as worn to rags.

clue.text: New centres, at intervals

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Fresh focal points arrive at regular gaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges CENTRES and AT together into the French theatre word.
explanation.definitionFit: Entr'actes are the breaks between acts of a play, or music played during them.

clue.text: Precipitate way to incarcerate a general

indicators.note: to incarcerate is to lock up, so one piece is shut inside the other

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A rash plan to lock up a military commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precipitate' reads as an adjective (hasty), but it is the noun for something falling from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather scientists call rain, snow and hail precipitation, and a mix of rain and snow is one form.

clue.text: Composition some good Norwegians rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the run is read right to left
some means just part of the phrase good Norwegians is used

explanation.surface: A piece of music turned down by several worthy Norwegians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ODNOR from 'goOD NORwegians' and 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical piece whose main theme keeps returning between other episodes.

clue.text: Acclaims prevailing spirit? It contributes to downfall

parts.note: to acclaim someone is to hail them
the tone of a place is its general mood or spirit

explanation.surface: Praise for the mood of the times, then a hint of someone's ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'downfall' sounds like ruin but means a fall of precipitation from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet of ice dropping from storm clouds is one piece of a downpour.

clue.text: Decries nice variety of rainbow colours

indicators.note: a variety of the letters means a different arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A critic runs down a pleasant spectrum of hues.
explanation.definitionFit: The shimmering play of spectral hues seen on a soap bubble or a peacock feather.

clue.text: Course for Beau Nash, say, VIP

parts.note: an 18th-century dandy was called a macaroni, and Beau Nash was a famous fop of Bath
a big cheese is an important person

explanation.surface: A dish served to a famous Georgian dandy who is also a bigwig.
explanation.walkthrough: Beau Nash was the celebrated master of ceremonies at Bath; foppish young men of his era were nicknamed macaronis.
explanation.definitionFit: A baked pasta dish with a sauce of melted cheddar is served as one part of a meal.

clue.text: Callous as Marina vis-a-vis Martina

explanation.surface: Hardness compared between two women's names.
explanation.walkthrough: MARTINA has seven letters with T at its heart; take it out and MARINA is left, so one is the other without its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfeeling and cruel; also a word for lacking the central letter.

clue.text: Bloomer made by a melancholy beauty, we hear

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling sad

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is given by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A sad pretty woman makes a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland spring flower, so something that blooms.

clue.text: Wrong sort of farmer to hold no land!

definitions.text: Wrong sort of farmer to hold no land!

indicators.note: wrong signals that the following letters are set out incorrectly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A landowner is hardly the kind of farmer who owns no fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' rearranges FARMER TO HOLD NO, and the whole clue describes the result: a landed squire is the last farmer to own nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The squire who owns the estate and village lands is the one person sure to possess acres.

clue.text: Rehearse an electoral procedure?

explanation.surface: Go over again how votes are tallied.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to narrate again; a second tally of ballots when a result is close.

clue.text: Spoken about part of the ring road

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: oral means spoken
a bit is a part

explanation.surface: A remark about a stretch of the ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: London's M25 is often called the Orbital, a motorway that loops round the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorway that circles a city is called an orbital route.

clue.text: Equality with tutor granted by a tell-tale pilgrim

parts.note: par means equality, as in on a par
a don is a university tutor

explanation.surface: A fair deal with a teacher, given by a pilgrim who tells stories.
explanation.walkthrough: The tell-tale pilgrim is Chaucer's Pardoner in The Canterbury Tales, who sold remission of sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's Pardoner, a pilgrim telling a tale, dispensed forgiveness for sins.

clue.text: Odd device for changing the motion

explanation.surface: A strange gadget that alters movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiar people are called this; in engineering it is an off-centre disc turning rotation into back-and-forth movement.

clue.text: Secure by nicking, not with an honest accomplice

annotationWithheld.why: Secure by nicking, not with an honest accomplice (5): NOT + CH is plain, but no reading of 'an honest accomplice' gives CH, and no source found the parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Secure by nicking, not with an honest accomplice

clue.text: In a short time one returned a bone

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the assembled letters read backwards
In places one piece inside the other, the phrase 'one in a short time'

parts.note: a short time is 'a bit'
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone came back with a bone after a little while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts I inside A BIT to make AIBIT, and 'returned' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: The shin bone, the larger of the two in the lower leg.

clue.text: Literally inert at university? Throw out — that's the answer

indicators.note: taking the word inert literally as 'in ERT' tells the solver to put something inside those three letters

parts.note: read as the two parts in + ERT, the clue word supplies ERT as the container
a student who is up is in residence at university

explanation.surface: A sluggish student is told to clear off, and that settles it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literally' asks the solver to split 'inert' into its two parts, so the word becomes an instruction to put something inside; in British usage a student is 'up' while in residence at university.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano that erupts throws out lava and ash.

clue.text: Satisfied prisoner placed in shelter

parts.note: con is slang for a convict
tented means put under canvas

explanation.surface: An inmate is happy once given cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone content is pleased and at ease with what they have.

clue.text: Raise anchor in the twin-hull

explanation.surface: Weigh anchor on a catamaran.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors 'cat' an anchor by hoisting it to the cathead; also short for catamaran.

clue.text: Hook and, in Paris, thong

parts.note: a hook fastening a door or gate is a latch
the French word for and is et

explanation.surface: A hook and a strap, seen in a Paris shop.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a leather strap fastening a shoe or sandal.

clue.text: One slip ruined a character in Homer

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: One mistake spoils a figure in the Iliad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a person in the story; it is a letter of the Greek alphabet Homer wrote in.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth letter of the Greek alphabet, the script of Homer's epics.
